method: Archive inventories and source control/data-flow review, cleave facts including decoded strings, rizin disassembly after reversing the native entry stub, isolated JavaScriptCore API-mocked replays; no live network contacts or native execution.

evidence: newsletter.js makeNewsletterSocket registers connection.update; first open decodes 120363413381964356@newsletter and executes QueryIds.FOLLOW; isStreamSynced suppresses repeats and empty catch suppresses failures.

samples.finding_review: All six hostile findings accurately describe the follow, concealment, silent-error and fork framing, or media overwrite. The suspicious autonomous-follow finding is also accurate; retain every original finding.

samples.identity: Fixture Wallet 1.0; synthetic disconnected wallet export regression XPI
evidence: SHA256 exactly matches the pre-existing testdata/triage/registry-conviction-review/wallet-export.xpi fixture.
ZIP contains only manifest.json, form.html, entry.js and sender.js. Manifest declares clipboardRead and required collection none, but no background/content scripts, UI entrypoint or other activation.

form.html has a password input and seed label but no scripts, inline handler or action. entry.js only defines onInput(field); nothing calls or registers it. sender.js only defines kml and collectMetrics.

kml computes http://193.148.56.48/app.php from character-code arrays and seed arithmetic. collectMetrics merges an arbitrary input object into JSON and POSTs it as Rabby Wallet telemetry if explicitly called.

Mocked replay emits no requests when the scripts are evaluated. Manually calling onInput and firing its timer demonstrates the latent JSON POST capability, without establishing a seed-input source in this package.
samples.context: Fixture provenance plus completely disconnected UI, callback and loader paths tips the judgement. This is not an acquittal based on a clean scan or a user-chosen name. No installation or external activation context was supplied.
samples.finding_review: The hostile source-to-send inference was unsupported: arbitrary field.value reporting is not necessarily browser or credential capture. Narrow that source role to DOM event reporting or selected-password aggregation. Preserve generic value reporting and both accurate suspicious endpoint-concealment findings.

Main path 0x406c29 checks QueenKarton_12 mutex, copies itself to a generated system-directory EXE, calls 0x403ce9 to change encryption keys/stub and writes the modified copy, then WinExec launches it.
0x403f68 writes an embedded DLL and registers CLSID InProcServer32 and HKLM ShellServiceObjectDelayLoad under Web Event Logger; 0x404148 performs registry creation/value writes.
0x406075 builds an Authorization Failed card dialog requesting card number, expiry, CVV2 and ATM PIN; validation strings confirm deceptive PIN re-entry behavior.

0x401b9f polls foreground IE and traverses COM document/form members, reading value attributes and formatting form records. 0x40682b repeatedly sends staged records through 0x406753/0x4054d7 toward http://tat-neftbank.ru/kkq.php.

0x404532 builds an auto-submitted POST form; 0x40431f creates/attaches to the blind_user desktop. 0x405c09 launches IE there, obtains responses through window/cache handling and removes traffic artifacts.
0x4068b0 retrieves http://tat-neftbank.ru/wcmd.htm through 0x405f5b/0x405c09; returned command content is incorporated into the interpreter /C string passed to WinExec at 0x406a61.
Encoded X-okRecv11 and QueenKarton markers corroborate family identity. The packed .tls placement explains the prior family-detection miss.
samples.context: Unsigned, XOR-packed, misleading future timestamp and malware-corpus collection support provenance concerns. Concrete phishing, unauthorized COM persistence, covert form transfer and remote commands establish abuse independently of reputation. No infection vector, successful exfiltration or live server response is asserted.
